questions.question: As a general rule of thumb in precis writing, the precis of a passage should be reduced to approximately what fraction of the original passage's length?

options.A: One-half
options.B: One-third
options.C: Two-thirds
options.D: One-tenth

questions.explanation: The conventional precis-writing rule is that the summary should be about one-third of the original passage's word count, which is why it is commonly called the 'one-third rule.'

questions.sub: What a precis is and is not
questions.question: A precis is best defined as:

options.A: A word-for-word copy of the most important sentences in a passage
options.B: A clear, coherent and condensed restatement of the substance of a passage in one's own words
options.C: A personal opinion piece written in response to a passage
options.D: An expanded version of the passage with additional examples

questions.explanation: By definition, a precis is a concise summary that captures the essential substance of the original in the writer's own words and coherent style; it is neither a verbatim extract, an opinion piece, nor an expansion.

questions.question: In precis writing, the "controlling idea" of a passage refers to:

options.A: The first sentence of the passage regardless of content
options.B: The central theme or main point around which all other details in the passage revolve
options.C: A minor illustrative detail mentioned only once
options.D: The concluding punctuation mark of the passage

questions.explanation: The controlling idea is the central, unifying theme that governs the passage's content; identifying it correctly is essential because the precis must be built around this idea, not around isolated details.

questions.question: While writing a precis, a candidate encounters a passage that repeats the same point three times using different examples and rhetorical flourishes for emphasis. The correct approach in the precis is to:

options.A: Reproduce all three examples to show thoroughness
options.B: State the point once in condensed form and omit the repeated illustrations and rhetorical flourishes
options.C: Omit the point entirely since it was repeated
options.D: Quote the most rhetorically striking example verbatim

questions.explanation: Precis writing requires stripping away repetition, illustration and rhetorical embellishment, retaining only the essential point stated once in condensed, plain language -- this is a core rule of the technique.

questions.question: When asked to supply a title for a precis, the most appropriate title is one that:

options.A: Is as long and descriptive as possible, summarising every sub-point
options.B: Is short, precise, and captures the central theme of the passage
options.C: Is copied directly from the passage's first sentence
options.D: Is deliberately vague so it could apply to any passage

questions.explanation: A good precis title should be brief yet accurately reflect the passage's central theme; it should neither be an overlong description nor so vague as to be meaningless, and need not be lifted from the passage.

questions.question: If the original passage for precis writing is written in the first person ("I believe...", "We argue..."), the standard convention for the precis is to:

options.A: Retain the first person exactly as in the original
options.B: Convert it into the third person and indirect/reported form
options.C: Switch to the second person throughout
options.D: Use a mix of first and second person randomly

questions.explanation: Standard precis-writing convention requires converting first-person or direct statements into third-person, reported (indirect) form, presenting the passage's substance objectively rather than retaining the original speaker's voice.

questions.question: A passage for precis writing is 450 words long. Following the standard one-third rule, the precis should ideally be closest to:

options.A: 450 words
options.B: 150 words
options.C: 50 words
options.D: 300 words

questions.explanation: One-third of 450 words is 150 words, so the precis should be written to approximately that length; a candidate must count words rather than estimate to keep the precis within the permitted range.

questions.question: In examinations, if the prescribed word limit for a precis is given as a range (for example, 100-120 words), a precis that is only 60 words long, even if accurate, will typically be marked down because:

options.A: Shorter answers are always preferred by examiners
options.B: It falls outside the prescribed word-count discipline and likely omits necessary substance
options.C: It uses too many words
options.D: Word count is never actually checked

questions.explanation: Precis writing enforces strict word-count discipline; falling well below the prescribed range usually signals that essential content has been omitted, and marks are deducted for not adhering to the specified limit.

questions.sub: What a precis is and is not
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a characteristic that a good precis should have?

options.A: Coherence and logical flow between ideas
options.B: Faithfulness to the original passage's meaning and proportion of emphasis
options.C: Insertion of the writer's own new arguments not present in the original
options.D: Conciseness within the prescribed word limit

questions.explanation: A precis must faithfully condense the original passage without adding the writer's own new arguments, opinions, or information not present in the source -- doing so is a common and penalised error, unlike coherence, faithfulness, and conciseness which are required qualities.

questions.question: Precis writing generally requires that the summary be written:

options.A: In note form using bullet points and abbreviations
options.B: As a single connected paragraph in plain, simple prose
options.C: In verse or poetic form for readability
options.D: As a series of unrelated one-line statements

questions.explanation: A precis is conventionally written as continuous, connected prose in a single paragraph using plain and simple language, not as bullet points, notes, or disconnected statements.

questions.question: In a precis, a sentence of direct speech such as He said, "I am very tired today" would most correctly be rendered as:

options.A: He said, "I am very tired today."
options.B: He said that he was very tired that day
options.C: He says he is very tired today
options.D: I am very tired today, he said

questions.explanation: Precis convention requires converting direct speech into third-person reported form, shifting the pronoun ('I' to 'he'), the tense ('am' to 'was' after a past reporting verb), and the time word ('today' to 'that day'); only option B applies all these changes.

questions.question: A passage set for precis is 240 words long. Applying the standard one-third rule, the precis should be closest to:

options.A: 240 words
options.B: 80 words
options.C: 160 words
options.D: 24 words

questions.explanation: One-third of 240 is 80, so the precis should be approximately 80 words; 160 is two-thirds, 24 is one-tenth, and 240 is the original length -- none of which follows the one-third rule.

questions.question: By convention, the title of a precis is:

options.A: Written above the precis and normally not counted in the prescribed word limit
options.B: Written at the very end and always counted in the word limit
options.C: Never permitted; a precis must have no title
options.D: Required to be identical to the first sentence of the passage

questions.explanation: A precis is conventionally given a short title placed above it, and this title is normally not included in the counted word limit of the precis itself; it need not repeat the first sentence and is not forbidden.

questions.sub: What a precis is and is not
questions.question: Which of the following should a candidate do FIRST when attempting a precis?

options.A: Begin writing the summary immediately from the first sentence onward
options.B: Read the whole passage carefully to grasp its central idea before writing anything
options.C: Count the words of the passage and stop reading at one-third of the way through
options.D: Copy the opening and closing sentences to use as the precis

questions.explanation: The correct first step in precis writing is to read the entire passage carefully to understand its central idea and overall meaning; only after grasping the whole can a faithful, proportionate summary be written.

questions.question: A passage argues that regular physical exercise improves not only bodily health but also memory, mood and sleep, and it illustrates each benefit with a study. Which of the following best states the controlling idea a precis should be built around?

options.A: The names and dates of the individual studies cited
options.B: Regular exercise brings wide-ranging benefits, both physical and mental
options.C: One study found that exercise improves sleep quality
options.D: Exercise is popular among young people

questions.explanation: The controlling idea is the central theme that unifies the passage -- that regular exercise yields broad physical and mental benefits; the individual studies are illustrative details, and option D is not supported by the passage.

questions.question: If a passage for precis is written in the first-person plural ("We believe...", "Our view is..."), the pronouns should typically be converted in the precis to:

options.A: The second person ("you")
options.B: The third person ("they", "their")
options.C: Retained unchanged as "we" and "our"
options.D: Removed so that no pronouns appear at all

questions.explanation: As with first-person singular, first-person plural pronouns are converted to the third person ('they', 'their') in a precis so that the summary reports the passage's substance objectively rather than in the original speaker's voice.

questions.question: A passage supports its single main claim with three statistical examples and a lengthy anecdote. In the precis, these examples and the anecdote should generally be:

options.A: Reproduced in full to demonstrate the writer's evidence
options.B: Condensed or omitted, since a precis keeps the essential point and drops illustrative detail
options.C: Expanded with additional examples of the candidate's own
options.D: Placed in a separate second paragraph after the precis

questions.explanation: A precis retains only the essential idea and normally drops illustrations, examples, statistics used merely to illustrate, and anecdotes; reproducing them in full, adding new ones, or appending them defeats the purpose of condensation.

questions.sub: What a precis is and is not
questions.question: A good precis should preserve which of the following from the original passage?

options.A: Its exact wording and sentence order
options.B: The relative emphasis and logical sequence of its main ideas
options.C: Every example and figure it contains
options.D: The writer's rhetorical questions and exclamations

questions.explanation: While a precis uses the writer's own words and is much shorter, it must keep the original's relative proportion of emphasis and the logical order of its main ideas so that no point is over- or under-stated; it does not preserve exact wording, all examples, or rhetorical flourishes.

questions.question: The one-third rule in precis writing is best understood as:

options.A: A rigid legal requirement that a precis be exactly one-third of the original to the word
options.B: A general guideline that a precis should be roughly one-third of the original passage's length
options.C: A rule that a precis should be three times longer than the passage
options.D: A rule requiring exactly three sentences in every precis

questions.explanation: The one-third rule is a rule of thumb, not an exact legal measure: the precis should be approximately one-third of the original length. It does not demand exact word-for-word thirds, an expanded version, or a fixed number of sentences.

questions.question: When a first-person passage is recast into reported form for a precis and the reporting is understood in the past, a present-tense verb such as "believes" in the original will normally become:

options.A: "will believe"
options.B: "believed"
options.C: "is believing"
options.D: "believe"

questions.explanation: In the third-person reported form used for precis, present-tense verbs normally shift back one tense to the past; 'believes' becomes 'believed', consistent with reporting the passage's substance indirectly.
